item.research_question: What are the structural, magnetic, and transport properties of the new equimolar high-entropy alloy FeRhIrPdPt, and how do its dual-phase microstructure and constituent binary alloys explain its magnetic behavior?
item.processing_route: Arc melting of constituent elements (Fe, Rh, Ir, Pd, Pt) with 99.9% purity in an Ar atmosphere to form 1.5 g button-shaped samples, followed by quenching on a water-chilled Cu hearth and multiple remelting cycles for homogeneity; no heat treatment or deformation applied.
item.test_conditions: XRD with Cu-Kα radiation; SEM/EDX at room temperature; DC magnetic susceptibility (χdc) between 50–450 K and 2 K; AC magnetic susceptibility (χac) between 3–300 K at frequencies 20 Hz–5 kHz; Electrical resistivity (ρ) between 3–300 K using a dc four-probe method.
key_findings: The alloy forms a dual-phase fcc structure with a Rh- and Ir-rich main phase (70 vol.%) and a Pd- and Pt-rich minor phase (30 vol.%).
The main phase is responsible for a canonical spin-glass transition at approximately 90 K.
The minor phase is responsible for a ferromagnetic correlation that appears below 300 K.
FeRh4 and FeIr4 binary alloys exhibit spin-freezing behavior, while FePd4 and FePt4 are ferromagnetic with Curie temperatures of ~400 K and ~317 K, respectively.
The effective magnetic moment (μeff) for FeRhIrPdPt is 3.40 μB/Fe, with a positive Weiss temperature (ΘCW) of 308 K indicating FM correlation.
The Mydosh parameter K for FeRhIrPdPt is 0.007, classifying it as a canonical spin-glass HEA.
Electrical resistivity of FeRhIrPdPt slightly increases on cooling, indicating weak carrier localization, unlike the metallic behavior of the binary alloys.
The dual-phase formation is explained by the pairwise formation enthalpies, where Fe-Pd and Fe-Pt pairings are more robust than Fe-Rh and Fe-Ir.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the dual-phase microstructure results from the thermodynamic preference for specific binary pairings (Fe-Pd, Fe-Pt, Ir-Rh) based on negative formation enthalpies. The magnetic properties arise from the independent contributions of the two phases: the Rh/Ir-rich main phase (analogous to FeRh4/FeIr4) drives the spin-glass transition at 90 K, while the Pd/Pt-rich minor phase (analogous to FePd4/FePt4) drives the ferromagnetic correlation below 300 K. The lack of long-range ordering in the ferromagnetic correlation is attributed to the inhomogeneous magnetic state of the minor phase.
item.limitations: The study was limited to as-cast samples without heat treatment or deformation; the thermal stability of the dual-phase microstructure was not investigated.
item.future_work: The authors state it is important to understand the thermal stability of the alloy to control the microstructure, and to investigate the possibility of multifunctional magnetic properties where the two phases offer different functions.
quotes: The dual-phase is composed of a Rh- and Ir-rich main phase and a Pd- and Pt-rich minor one.
One is the canonical spin-glass transition at 90 K, and the other is a ferromagnetic correlation that appears below 300 K.
The main and minor phases were responsible for the spin-glass transition and the ferromagnetic correlation below 300 K, respectively.
